issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int (total number of students). The solution implementation instead defines getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object (a custom wrapper class) and provides a StudentCount class in the solution repository. This introduces a mismatched return type between the specification and the provided solution and adds a class (StudentCount) that is not mentioned in the problem statement or the template. Students following the problem/UML will implement an int-returning method, but the reference solution uses a different type, which is likely to confuse students and could cause tests or autograding that expect an int to fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred correction: change the solution to match the UML/spec and have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (the sum of inscribed and guest students). Remove the StudentCount class from the solution (or keep it only if documented). Alternative correction: if the intent is to use a StudentCount wrapper, update the problem statement (UML, task text) and the template to declare/describe StudentCount and change the UML method return type to StudentCount, and include a StudentCount class stub in the template repository so students see and use it.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a primitive int (the total number of students). The solution, however, introduces a new StudentCount class and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount instance. This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) and changes the expected type for the same conceptual entity (the total number of students). Students reading the problem/template expect an int result and will be confused by the solution returning an object type and by the additional method calls (e.g. getValue()) required to obtain the numeric count.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem/template by making getTotalNumberOfStudents() return a primitive int (the sum of inscribed and guest students). Remove or keep StudentCount only as an internal helper if desired, but do not expose it as the public return type. Update getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() accordingly to use the int return value (e.g. use getTotalNumberOfStudents() directly). Alternatively, if the StudentCount abstraction is intentionally required, update the problem statement and UML to specify StudentCount as the return type and document its API — but the simpler fix is to change the solution to return int to match the exercise description.
